question.leadin: Answer the following about Douglas MacArthur.
question.text: Truman dismissed Douglas MacArthur and replaced him with Matthew Ridgway during this war. MacArthur led a surprise amphibious landing at Incheon (IN-chon) during this war.
question.clue: The Armistice Agreement that ended this war was signed shortly after Joseph Stalin's death caused a withdrawal of Soviet support.

swap.leadin: Name these dictators who are still alive.
swap.text: This man assumed leadership of North Korea in 1997. He has insisted on the right to nuclear power and oversaw the imprisonment of two American journalists last summer.
swap.clue: His "Sunshine policy" tried to bolster the software industry, and he once abducted a movie director to shoot a socialist Godzilla flick.

question.text: The Tibetan invasion wasn't the only Chinese invasion of the 1950s; they also invaded Korea after the US and South Korean forces almost crossed this river, the border between China and Korea.
question.clue: The Friendship Bridge is the only remaining bridge over this river and connects the cities of Dandong and Sinujiu.

swap.leadin: This nation's leader was appointed the Supreme People's Assembly in an election in which no one allegedly voted "no"
swap.text: Name this country which, in 2011, saw the appointment of Kim Jong-Un as Supreme Leader following the death of his father Kim Jong-Il.
swap.clue: One leader threatened this country with "fire and fury like the world has never seen."

question.text: Yi utilized ships named for these animals, which some say is an early type of ironclad. Those ships had armor that was said to resemble these animals' shells.
question.clue: Soldiers from Ming China helped defend Korea from Japanese invasion at the end of the 16th century. During that conflict, Korean Admiral Yi utilized these crazy awesome vessels which received their name from the appearance caused by their armored decks.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the abolition of slavery throughout the world.
swap.text: This dynasty abolished slavery in Korea as part of the Gabo Reforms in 1894. This dynasty declared Korea an empire in 1897; however, it would be annexed to the Japanese empire in 1910.
swap.clue: This dynasty was destabilized by succession crises called the Strifes of the Princes.

question.text: With Goguryeo and Baekje, this kingdom that called itself Geunhwahyang was one of Korea's three kingdoms. A pseudo-military unit in this kingdom was the hwarang, its "flowering knights."
question.clue: This dynasty employed a cultured class of cosmetic-using soldiers called the "flowering knights," or "hwarang."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about numerically-named periods of Chinese history.
swap.text: Cao Cao, Sun Quan, and Liu Bei fought for control of China during this era between the Han and Jin Dynasties. It is the namesake of a novel by Luo Guanzhong.
swap.clue: The "Later" part of a period with this name was dominated by a Unified Silla that conquered Goguryeo.

question.leadin: Among this man's domestic accomplishments include granting serfs a form of maternity leave and backing the development of the world's first rain gauge.
question.text: Identify this fourth ruler of Korea's Joseon (JOH-sun) dynasty whose establishment of the 28-letter hangul script is still celebrated on an October holiday.
question.clue: Under the guidance of his father, this man launched an expedition against a polity controlled by So Sadashige that had become a base for pirates; that assault on Tsushima was the Oei invasion.

swap.leadin: In 1968, this country's president was almost killed in an incident named for the residence of this country's leader.
swap.text: Name this country, whose leader lives in the Blue House. In 1953, this country was split from its communist northern neighbor by a demilitarized zone.
swap.clue: Its first president brutally suppressed the Jeju Uprising before being ousted in the April 19 Movement.

question.leadin: For one of these groups to be officially recognized by the Court of the Lord Lyon, it must have a chief.
question.text: What are these kinship groups in which members often took the chief's surname and which often have a distinctive tartan pattern?
question.clue: What name is given to these family and extended groups identified by their differing tartans?

swap.leadin: This kingdom's ruler Gwanggaeto the Great erected a massive stele on the banks of the Yalu River detailing its history.
swap.text: Name this northernmost of Korea's Three Kingdoms, which repelled an invading Sui Dynasty army of more than 300,000 soldiers by drowning almost all of them at the Battle of the Salsu River.
swap.clue: Some of the best-preserved art of this kingdom survives in the tomb of Dong Shou at a complex at Anak.

question.text: Kublai installed prince Wonjong [wun-JOHNG] as the ruler of this peninsula's Goryeo [kor-yuh] dynasty, allowing the Mongols to use it to launch two failed invasions of Japan. The Goryeo lend this peninsula its English name.
question.clue: The "Three Kingdoms" of this region included Baekje, Silla, and Goguryeo.

swap.text: Before his assassination, Park Chung Hee led South Korea through an economic miracle named for this river that flows through Seoul.

question.leadin: The Haerye ("HEH-r'yeh") commentary helps explain how to use this system, whose creation is commemorated by a national holiday on October 9.
question.text: Name this system said to be easy enough to understand that even a stupid man could learn how to use it in ten days.
question.answerHtml: Hangul [or Hangeul; or Chosongeul; accept Korean alphabet or Korean script; prompt on Korean; prompt on alphabet or script]
question.clue: This alphabet is transliterated using the McCune-Reischauer system, and was banned under a cultural assimilation policy before the outbreak of World War II.

swap.text: The successful repulse of Japan extended the rule of this dynasty, under which the Hangul alphabet was created. It ruled until Japan finally conquered the peninsula in 1910.
swap.clue: Once led by Sejong the Great, this dynasty promulgated the hanggul script and pursued an isolationist policy that led it to be known as the "hermit kingdom."

question.text: A large stele named for this Goguryeo ("koh-GOOR-yaw") king was found in his tomb. Controversy exists over whether the "sinmyo" passage of that stele named for this king details the conquest of two Korean kingdoms by Goguryeo or Japan.
question.clue: This ruler adopted an era name translating to "eternal rejoicing," thus proclaiming that his kingdom was on equal standing with Chinese imperial dynasties.

swap.leadin: The Nihon Shoki credits this kingdom's monks with introducing Buddhism to Yamato and states that it sent herbalists to Emperor Kinmei in a request for military aid.
swap.text: Name this kingdom whose craftsmen built the Asuka-dera. Tang China allied with Silla ("SHILL-uh") and invaded this southwestern Korean kingdom in 660.
swap.clue: This kingdom absorbed all of the lands of the Mahan confederacy, thus seizing all of the present-day Jeolla ("jul-lah") region, under its great ruler Geunchogo ("geun-choh-goh").

question.text: A gold-and-jade antler crown was found outside of South Korean city, which holds the burial mounds of Silla kings. This site of the Hwabaek council was the capital of Silla.

swap.leadin: Early 20th century ultranationalist historian Shin Chaeho denounced this text for disregarding Manchurian kingdoms as ethnically-Korean, and affirming an ideology of servitude to China called sadaejuui.
swap.text: Name this 12th century text compiled by Kim Busik, the oldest extant chronicle of Korean history. A later text describes the "memorabilia" or yusa of the same era of history that this book records.
